{{short description|3D coordinate system used in mathematics}}
In [[mathematics]], '''6-sphere coordinates''' are a [[coordinate system]] for three-dimensional space obtained by [[Inversive geometry|inverting]] the 3D [[Cartesian coordinate system|Cartesian coordinates]] across the [[unit sphere|unit 2-sphere]] <math>x^2+y^2+z^2=1</math>.  They are so named because the [[locus (mathematics)|loci]] where one coordinate is constant form [[sphere]]s tangent to the [[Origin (mathematics)|origin]] from one of six sides (depending on which coordinate is held constant and whether its value is positive or negative). This coordinate system exists independently from and has no relation to the [[N-sphere|6-sphere]].
The three coordinates are
:<math>u = \frac{x}{x^2+y^2+z^2},\quad v = \frac{y}{x^2+y^2+z^2},\quad w = \frac{z}{x^2+y^2+z^2}.</math>
Since inversion is an [[Involution_(mathematics)|involution]], the equations for ''x'', ''y'', and ''z'' in terms of ''u'', ''v'', and ''w'' are similar:
:<math>x = \frac{u}{u^2+v^2+w^2},\quad y = \frac{v}{u^2+v^2+w^2},\quad z = \frac{w}{u^2+v^2+w^2}.</math>  
This coordinate system is [[Separable partial differential equation|<math>R</math>-separable]] for the 3-variable Laplace equation.
